summary: TRACK 6: confirmed missing-`re`-import bug is blocker-scoped to exactly 2/6 resources, 0/6 tools; found 3 additional confirmed-via-repro bugs (tracker insertion-order, regex-replacement-string injection into sw.js/tracker.md, live stats miscounting) plus JSON-RPC id-loss and silent-success-on-unknown-input gaps in process_request().
result_text:
TRACK 6 — Python automation & MCP server correctness. All findings verified by direct repro against a scratch copy of the real repo files (see method notes), not just code reading.

## 1. [BLOCKER] Missing `import re` — confirmed, full blast radius traced
mcp-server/site_mcp.py:28-31 imports only json/os/sys/Path. `re.finditer`/`re.sub` used at lines 215-216 (site://projects) and 224-225 (site://achievements). Grep-confirmed no `import re` anywhere in the file.
Not rescued transitively: scripts/site_automation.py:26 does `import re`, but site_mcp.py:39 does a plain `import site_automation` (not `from site_automation import *`), so that binds only the name `site_automation`, never `re`, in site_mcp.py's namespace.
Blast radius (traced call graph): exactly 2 of 6 resources are dead — site://projects and site://achievements always raise `NameError` on read, 100% of the time, no partial-success path. 0 of 6 tools are affected — `handle_tool_call()` (line 233) never calls `handle_resource_read()`; all 6 tools route only through `site_automation.*` functions. site://stats, site://health, site://tracker, site://graph are unaffected (no `re` usage in those branches).
Does NOT crash the server process: the NameError propagates uncaught through `process_request()` (no try/except there) up to `run_stdio_server()`'s outer `except Exception` (line 420-427), which converts it into a well-formed JSON-RPC error — but see #2, that response's `id` is wrong.
Fix: add `import re` at top of site_mcp.py.

## 2. [HIGH] process_request() error responses lose request `id` on every exception
mcp-server/site_mcp.py: neither the `resources/read` branch (line 307, calls `handle_resource_read` unguarded) nor `tools/call` (line 332, calls `handle_tool_call` unguarded) wraps its handler call in try/except. Any exception raised inside (bug #1's NameError, or any future exception — e.g. a subprocess failure, a missing tracker file, the re.error in #4b below) bubbles up to `run_stdio_server()`'s outer catch.
That catch has two branches: `except json.JSONDecodeError` (line 412, `id: None` is correct here — the id genuinely can't be recovered from unparseable JSON) vs `except Exception` (line 420-427, `id: None` hardcoded at line 423) — but at this point `request` *was* successfully parsed (line 407 ran before `process_request()` raised), so `request.get("id")` is available and simply not used. Every error surfaced this way returns `id: null` regardless of what the client sent, breaking JSON-RPC request/response correlation for that call.
Not hypothetical — bug #1 guarantees this triggers on ordinary, documented usage (any site://projects or site://achievements read).
Fix: in the `except Exception` block, do `req_id = locals().get("request", {}).get("id")` (or set `req_id = None` before the try and assign it right after `json.loads` succeeds) and use it instead of the literal `None`.

## 3. [HIGH] update_dev_tracker inserts new entries in the wrong position — confirmed via live repro
scripts/site_automation.py:161-183 `update_tracker()`. `insert_pos = content.find("\n\n- **", meta_idx)` (line 173) is meant to find "right after ## Meta," but the real tracker.md has only a single `\n` between `## Meta` and the first (current top) entry — the double-newline pattern instead matches the gap *between* the current top entry and the second entry. Repro (scratch copy of the live dev-logs/PortfolioWebsite_TRACKER.md, no repo file touched): calling `update_tracker("v47", "Test Insertion Order Probe", [...])` produced a file whose H1 (line 178's regex) correctly says `# Portfolio Website Tracker — v47`, but whose entry list still shows v46 first and v47 second — the tool's own two effects (title sync vs. entry insertion) contradict each other on the very next read. This reproduces on every normal call given the tracker's current (and only realistic, since it already has 46 versions) structure — not an edge case.
Fix: anchor insertion directly off `meta_idx + len("## Meta")` (skipping to the first newline after the header) rather than searching for a `"\n\n- **"` separator that happens to exist between entries 1 and 2.

## 4. [HIGH/MEDIUM] Unescaped `re.sub()` replacement strings — user-supplied `version` treated as a backreference template
Root cause (two call sites, two different failure modes):
**4a. sync_metadata() [HIGH]** — scripts/site_automation.py:146, `re.sub(r"(CACHE_NAME\s*=\s*['\"])[^'\"]+(['\"])", rf"\g<1>{cache_name}\g<2>", sw_text)`. `cache_name` embeds the caller-supplied `version_tag` unescaped inside the replacement-string, between two live `\g<n>` backreferences. Repro: `sync_metadata("46\\g<1>evil")` → `sync_site_metadata` tool → **no exception, reports success**, but sw.js's CACHE_NAME line becomes `const CACHE_NAME = 'aaradhya-portfolio-v46CACHE_NAME = 'evil';` — syntactically invalid JavaScript (stray unterminated string/bare identifier), which would break Service Worker registration site-wide if this working-tree file were committed and pushed. Mitigating factor: verify.py's existing JS-syntax check would likely catch this at sync.ps1's pre-commit gate if that workflow is followed — but the tool still corrupts the working file and reports false success regardless of whether the commit is gated.
**4b. update_tracker() [MEDIUM]** — scripts/site_automation.py:178, same pattern but the H1 pattern `r"# Portfolio Website Tracker — v\d+"` has zero capture groups. Repro: `update_tracker("v47\\1", ...)` → **raises `re.error: invalid group reference 1 at position 34`**, uncaught, surfaces as bug #2's generic `id: null` internal error. Happens before `TRACKER_MD.write_text()`, so unlike 4a this does not corrupt the file — but it's an ungraceful, unhelpful failure for a plausible fat-fingered input (a stray backslash-digit in a version string).
Fix: build the replacement via a `lambda m: ...` function instead of a template string (functions passed to `re.sub` bypass backreference parsing entirely), or `re.escape()` the interpolated value before use — note `re.escape()` on a *replacement* string doesn't fully neutralize `\g<n>`, so the lambda approach is the correct fix, not just escaping.

## 5. [MEDIUM-HIGH] update_dev_tracker's `highlights` are written into markdown with zero sanitization
scripts/site_automation.py:167, `highlights_md = "\n".join([f"  - {h}" for h in highlights])` — no escaping of markdown-active characters, and critically no rejection/escaping of literal newlines within a single highlight string. Repro: a highlight of `"evil\n\n## Meta\n- **INJECTED FAKE ENTRY** gotcha"` breaks out of its bullet scope and inserts a fabricated `## Meta` heading and a fabricated top-level entry directly into the tracker's permanent history, while `update_tracker()` still reports `success: true`. Checked whether this cascades further: it does not currently misdirect the *next* call's `meta_idx` anchor, since `content.find("## Meta")` (line 171) always returns the real (leftmost) header first — but the injected content itself permanently corrupts the historical record unless caught by manual diff review.
Fix: reject/strip newlines from each highlight element (or join safely per-element after replacing `\n` with a space), and consider escaping leading `#`/`-`/`*` at the start of a highlight line.

## 6. [MEDIUM/HIGH] Unknown-input branches return "successful" JSON-RPC results instead of error objects
- Unknown `tools/call` name → site_mcp.py:264-265, `handle_tool_call()` returns the plain string `"Unknown tool: {name}"`, which `process_request()`'s `tools/call` branch (line 329-344) wraps as an ordinary, non-error `result.content[0].text`. No JSON-RPC `error`, no MCP `isError: true` flag — a client that checks the conventional `isError` field to detect tool failure will read this as a successful completion. [medium]
- Unknown `resources/read` uri → site_mcp.py:229-230, same pattern via `handle_resource_read()`'s fallback. [medium]
- Unknown `prompts/get` name → site_mcp.py:353-361 — worse than the above two: `else: prompt_text = "Perform SEO and structured metadata audit..."` (line 359-360) silently substitutes the *other*, unrelated, valid prompt (`audit-seo-metadata`) for **any** unrecognized `prompt_name`, with zero error signal of any kind. A caller with a typo'd or stale prompt name gets a plausible-looking but wrong prompt back, which could mislead an agent into acting on unintended instructions. [high]
Fix: populate the JSON-RPC `error` field (or MCP's `isError: true` result flag for tools) for unknown tool/resource/prompt names instead of a descriptive-string "success".

## 7. [HIGH] get_site_stats() / get_site_telemetry — confirmed live miscounts, not malformed-input-dependent
scripts/site_automation.py:101 & 105. Verified against the actual repo HTML (not hypothetical):
- **project_count** (line 101): `re.findall(r'class="project-card', content)` also matches the per-card inner wrapper `class="project-card-body"` (30 of these exist, one per project) in addition to the 30 real `.project-card` wrappers — grep-confirmed 60 total substring matches vs. 30 actual project cards. **Reports exactly 2x the true count, today, with default input.**
- **achievement_count** (line 105): primary selector `class="achievement-card` matches **zero** elements — the real wrapper class in achievements.html is `achievement-item`, not `achievement-card` (stale/wrong selector). This falls through the `or` to the fallback `class="cert-btn` (53 matches: some achievement cards have 2 `cert-btn` elements for multi-photo certs), when the true achievement count is 37 (confirmed via `achievement-item reveal`, `achievement-title` — all 37). **Reports 53 vs. actual 37 (+43%), today, with default input.**
These feed directly into both `site://stats` and the `get_site_telemetry` tool.
Fix: match the actual wrapper classes precisely (`class="project-card reveal` / `class="project-card reveal` with word-boundary, and `class="achievement-item` instead of `achievement-card`), or better, count a structurally-unique per-card marker (e.g. `data-` attribute) rather than a `class=` substring prone to matching child elements.

## 8. [LOW] mcp_config.json hardcodes a personal absolute path
mcp-server/mcp_config.json:6 — `"d:/Aaradhya-Dev-Tamrakar/Aaradhya-Dev-Tamrakar.github.io/mcp-server/site_mcp.py"`. Committed to the public repo; won't work on any other machine/OS (or Aaradhya's own machine if the drive letter/path ever changes) without manual edit. Not a security leak (mirrors the public repo name), just a portability gap.
Fix: relative path or environment/workspace-variable if the target MCP client (Claude Desktop/Cursor/Antigravity) supports one.

## 9. [NIT] run_verification's `verbose` arg has no type check
site_mcp.py:236 → scripts/site_automation.py:62-66, `if verbose:` on a raw arg. A caller passing the JSON string `"false"` (not boolean `false`) would be treated as truthy and unexpectedly enable `--verbose`.

## 10. [OBSERVATION] MCP tool layer doesn't replicate the CLI layer's own required-arg validation
scripts/site_automation.py:196, 199-201 — `main()`'s argparse correctly marks `--version`/`--title`/`--highlights` `required=True` and cleanly fails with a usage error if omitted via CLI. But site_mcp.py's `handle_tool_call()` (lines 249, 254-256, using `args.get(key, "")`/`args.get(key, [])`) does not enforce the `"required"` arrays each tool already declares in its own `inputSchema` (site_mcp.py:129, 152) — missing required fields silently default to empty string/list instead of erroring. This is the direct enabling condition for #4 and #5 above: a request with `"version"` simply omitted proceeds with `version=""` rather than failing fast with a clear "missing required field" error.
Fix: validate `args` against each tool's own `inputSchema["required"]` list at the top of `handle_tool_call()` before dispatching.

## Method notes
All repro'd bugs (3, 4a, 4b, 5, 7) were run against scratch copies of the real repo files (`/tmp/tracker_scratch*.md`, `/tmp/sw_scratch.js`) via `site_automation`'s actual functions with `TRACKER_MD`/`SW_JS` monkey-patched to the scratch paths — no files in the working repo were modified, no commits made, sync.ps1 not invoked, per track scope.
